title: Frequency-specific temporal identifiability sweep -- pre-P4 requirement (Hamm)
notes: Purpose: before any band-specific SPK-LFP lag is interpreted, empirically determine each band's actual temporal resolution using the EXACT causal pipeline (causal_envelope + lagged_association), not a simplified proxy. See omission/jnwb_ext/identifiability.py for the full synthesis/recovery/summary code.

Design: synthetic true band-state S(t) (smooth AR(1)-power process) drives a spike-rate proxy R(t) at a KNOWN true_delay_ms (both signs tested: LFP-leads-spike and spike-leads-LFP). Raw LFP is built by amplitude-modulating a band-center carrier by sqrt(S(t)). causal_envelope is applied to the raw LFP exactly as it would be on real data, producing P_hat(t), which itself lags true S(t) by the band's own effective_latency_ms. lagged_association(P_hat, R) is then run over lags in [-1000,1000]ms at 5ms resolution.

FINDING 1 (confirms Hamm's prediction, now quantified): recovered NOMINAL lag is systematically biased by approximately -effective_latency_ms for every band (mean_bias_ms column tracks -effective_latency_ms closely: high_gamma -41.2 vs -48.8 latency, low_gamma -64.8 vs -68.8, beta -121.7 vs -125.8, alpha -197.3 vs -205.8, theta -362.0 vs -393.8 [theta's mean is outlier-corrupted, see Finding 2]). p_correct_sign_nominal (naive reading of raw recovered lag's sign as the directional answer) is poor for every band (0.56-0.79) -- NOT because the estimator can't detect directionality, but because a true delay smaller than the band's own effective latency still produces a negative nominal lag. This is the exact conflation risk flagged in review: nominal lag sign alone must never be read as physiological lead/lag without first subtracting the band's own effective_latency_ms.

FINDING 1 continued: p_correct_sign_latency_corrected (sign of recovered_lag_ms + effective_latency_ms, i.e. correcting for the estimator's own known constant latency before asking about directionality) is good for every band except theta: high_gamma 0.95, low_gamma 1.00, beta 0.95, alpha 0.89, theta 0.89. So Estimand-A-style directional recovery (does past band state predict subsequent firing, in which direction) is viable for ALL bands once the known bias is corrected -- this is the basis for keeping all bands in Estimand A while restricting fine ms-scale Estimand B claims to fast bands only.

FINDING 2 (new, more serious than a simple 'theta is coarser' story): theta's peak-argmax lag recovery is genuinely MULTIMODAL, not just noisier. At n_repeats=8 several conditions showed wild single-repeat outliers 400-900ms from the rest of the cluster (e.g. true_delay=5ms: 7/8 repeats clustered near a corrected value close to the true delay, 1/8 landed ~570ms away with a NEGATIVE peak correlation -- an anti-correlated spurious match, not noise around the right answer). At n_repeats=20 (final run, see identifiability_sweep_raw_20260827.csv/identifiability_sweep_summary_20260827.csv), theta's median_abs_deviation_from_true_ms is 8.8ms -- comparable to other bands' typical performance -- but outlier_fraction_gt_median_plus_5mad is 0.08 (8% of trials), which inflates theta's mean_bias_ms and zero_delay_corrected_sd_ms (392.9ms) far beyond what a Gaussian-noise model would predict. A mean/SD-only summary would badly misrepresent theta's actual behavior -- report median/MAD alongside mean/SD for this band, and flag that theta's min_resolvable_delay_ms could not be computed by the SD-based criterion (denominator inflated by outlier contamination) though the median-based picture suggests theta IS typically usable at the tested delay grid, contingent on an outlier-resistant aggregation strategy for any downstream analysis (e.g. across-trial median lag rather than mean, or explicit outlier rejection).

min_resolvable_delay_ms (per-band, smallest tested |true_delay_ms| where a signed direction's corrected-recovered-delay distribution separates from the delay=0 distribution by >1 zero-delay SD): high_gamma 5ms, low_gamma 5ms, beta 5ms, alpha 5ms, theta NaN (SD-based criterion breaks down under theta's outlier contamination; see Finding 2). This is a conservative, explicit, reportable criterion -- not a claim of a sharp physical detection limit -- and is itself contingent on aggregation method (mean vs median) for theta specifically.

Estimand A vs B implication (direct application of Hamm's required framework): Estimand A (does past band-specific LFP state predict subsequent firing, reported with temporal support/latency, no ms-resolved claim) is supported for ALL FIVE bands given latency-corrected sign accuracy 0.89-1.00. Estimand B (fine tens-of-ms temporal ordering) is only defensible for high_gamma/low_gamma/beta given their tight, low-outlier-fraction, ~5-10ms resolution; alpha is borderline (SD=4.97ms at zero-delay is tight, but effective_latency itself is 206ms, so any single-trial ms-scale claim must carry that latency alongside it); theta should NOT be used for Estimand B without an outlier-resistant estimator and larger-N averaging -- its raw single-estimate reliability is compromised by the ~8% catastrophic-failure rate found here.

issues.description: The simple argmax(|lagged_association|) peak-picking estimator used here and in the P0 prototype (omission/jnwb_ext/lag_estimation.py) is vulnerable to locking onto a spurious secondary/sidelobe correlation peak for theta, at an empirically measured rate of ~8% per single-trial estimate (n=20 repeats per condition, 2026-08-27 sweep).
issues.action: before any theta-band lag claim (even a coarse one) is reported from real data, either (a) aggregate across many trials with a robust statistic (median, trimmed mean) rather than a single-trial peak, or (b) add an explicit peak-quality gate (e.g. require peak correlation magnitude well above a null-calibrated threshold, reject negative-correlation 'peaks' as spurious) before accepting a single-trial theta lag estimate. Not yet implemented -- flagging for the P4 estimator design, not fixed here (this module is the identifiability characterization, not the scientific estimator).

verification.status: CONFIRMED (2026-08-27) -- independent verifier recomputed all four headline claims directly from identifiability_sweep_raw_20260827.csv (not from this session's summary CSV/JSON) and independently traced the bias-direction math. (1) bias_ms tracking -effective_latency_ms: confirmed per-band, matches to within 5-10% (expected from 5ms lag-grid discretization + noise). (2) p_correct_sign_nominal (0.56-0.79) and p_correct_sign_latency_corrected (0.89-1.00): both recomputed independently from raw rows, match reported values exactly. (3) theta's ~8% outlier fraction: confirmed NOT an artifact of the median+5*MAD formula -- an independent, more conventional Tukey IQR (Q3+1.5*IQR) criterion gives 8.3% vs the reported 8.0%; theta's max single-trial deviation (1583.8ms) vs 8.8-75.8ms for every other band was confirmed a qualitatively distinct heavy tail, not merely wider Gaussian noise. (4) min_resolvable_delay_ms values reproduced exactly by re-running summarize_sweep on the raw CSV; code review confirmed the +/- pooling bug (found and fixed mid-session) is genuinely absent from the current file. Sign-convention/direction check: traced concretely through one row (high_gamma, true_delay=100ms, repeat 0: recovered=60.0ms, eff_lat=48.83ms, corrected=108.8ms ~= true 100ms) -- confirmed the bias-correction direction (recovered + effective_latency_ms) is correct, not backwards. No code defects found beyond the already-flagged, still-open theta peak-picking multimodality issue.
verification.self_verification_done: sweep design, recovery code, and summary statistics were iteratively corrected during this session's own build: (1) an initial p_correct_sign metric conflated nominal-lag sign with latency-corrected sign, producing misleadingly low numbers for well-behaved bands -- fixed by separating the two; (2) an initial min_resolvable_delay_ms pooled +delay and -delay by absolute value, corrupting the separation statistic since they sit on opposite sides of the bias baseline -- fixed to compute per-signed-direction; (3) an n_repeats=8 first pass showed anomalously high SD for theta driven by rare severe outliers -- re-run at n_repeats=20 with added median/MAD/outlier-fraction statistics to characterize this properly rather than reporting a misleading mean/SD summary.
